fullText:
Summary: ACL Cables PLC (ACL.N0000), Sri Lanka's largest cable maker, is a well-run, cash-rich business: return on equity has averaged about 21% over five years, it holds about Rs 10.9bn more cash and investments than debt, and it hasn't made a loss in ten years. Profit to owners rose 38% to Rs 6.34bn in the year to March 2026 (EPS Rs 8.82 after the 1-for-3 share split) and another 15% in April–June 2026. But the share has roughly doubled in a year: at Rs 100 (end of June; check the live price) it trades at about 11x trailing earnings and 1.85x its NAV of Rs 54.04, while its own ten-year average P/E is about 5.5x. Earnings ride on high copper prices and exchange gains, and very little profit is turned into cash or paid out (dividends about 6% of profit). The methods put fair value at about Rs 63.50, so the price is roughly 55% above it. I'd buy at up to about Rs 54 and treat under Rs 47.60 as a strong buy.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 100.00 (last traded, 30 June 2026, from the interim report). Please check it live. In April–June 2026 it traded between Rs 85.00 and Rs 103.50; the January–March 2026 high was Rs 107.75.
Three months to 30 June 2026 (unaudited): revenue Rs 11.49bn (up 17%), gross profit Rs 2.78bn (down 5%, margin 24% against 30%), profit to owners Rs 1.84bn (up 15%), EPS Rs 2.56 (Rs 2.24). Net finance income was Rs 806mn, including a Rs 590mn exchange gain.
Year to March 2026 (audited): revenue Rs 45.51bn (up 21%), profit after tax Rs 7.28bn, profit to owners Rs 6.34bn, EPS Rs 8.82 (Rs 6.37 split-adjusted), ROE about 19%. Trailing EPS is about Rs 9.14.
NAV Rs 54.04 a share (June 2026). Shares in issue 718.7 million after the 1-for-3 split. Majority owned by the Madanayake family (about 62%).

Valuation table (Rs per share)
Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted
Justified P/B | 36.0 | 56.7 | 87.8 | 56.7
P/E | 42.0 | 72.0 | 105.0 | 69.6
Residual income | 32.0 | 61.0 | 121.7 | 64.4
Average | 36.7 | 63.3 | 104.8 | 63.6
Fair value about Rs 63.50 (30% bear, 50% base, 20% bull). Buy at up to Rs 54.00 (15% below); strong buy under Rs 47.60 (25% below).

Assumptions
Cost of equity 18% / 16.5% / 15%, against government bonds of about 12%. Long-run ROE 14% / 17% / 20% (five-year average about 21%, including an unusually strong 2022/23 when the gross margin reached 36%). Growth 6% / 6.5% / 7%. EPS to March 2027 Rs 7.00 / 9.00 / 10.50, valued at 6 / 8 / 10 times.

What stands out
- Strong balance sheet: about Rs 15.2bn of unit trusts, deposits and cash against Rs 4.3bn of debt.
- Weak cash conversion: over the last two years operating cash flow was Rs 5.4bn against Rs 12.7bn of profit; stock and receivables keep growing with copper prices. In April–June 2026 inventory alone rose Rs 4.5bn.
- Tiny payout: about Rs 359mn of dividends a year against Rs 6bn+ of profit to owners.
- Part of recent profit is exchange gains (Rs 500mn in 2025/26, Rs 590mn in one quarter this year), which can reverse.

500-share plan
200 shares up to Rs 63.50, 150 up to Rs 54.00, 150 up to Rs 47.60: average about Rs 55.90, about Rs 27,940 in total. Rs 54 needs about a 46% fall from Rs 100. Allowing for the split, the share was about Rs 41 in March 2025, so these prices are recent history, but getting back there would probably need a copper or market downturn.

What would change my view
Higher: copper staying high without hurting demand, exports growing 30%+, a much bigger dividend, ROE above 20% without exchange gains.
Lower: a copper price fall (inventory losses, as in 2023/24), less power and construction spending, more borrowing to carry stock, a stronger rupee.

Business tests: 3 of 4 passed (returns, debt, steady profit; fails on cash conversion), so it's a good business at a high price: watch list.
